# **Forensic Audit of RS-Quant and Architectural Blueprint for a Self-Recursively Improving Multi-Asset Trading System on Bitget**

## **Executive System Audit and Structural Diagnosis**

The engineering evolution of QuantDesk (project name RS-Quant) between September 24, 2026, and October 14, 2026, demonstrates an uncommon commitment to software verification, deterministic replay, and scientific falsification1. Across roughly 175 Python modules and 950 automated unit, integration, and research tests enforced via static type checking (mypy) and linting (ruff), the system has successfully transitioned from an unverified, state-corrupted prototype into a clean, fail-closed paper execution environment1. The remediation of silent accounting distortions—specifically the omission of entry fees in research records that obscured nearly half of realized losses (-193.29 USDT reported versus \-302.99 USDT actual), the misapplication of maker fees (0.02%) to market stop-out orders (0.06%), the absence of perpetual funding settlements, and multi-writer parameter collisions—establishes a trustworthy observational baseline1.  
Despite this high engineering discipline, the empirical record reveals a fundamental structural divide between software correctness and quantitative edge1. The initial "Unified Agentic Alpha Engine" failed not because of implementation bugs, but because its architecture violated the core law of market microstructure: expected gross alpha over the holding horizon must strictly exceed the sum of exchange transaction fees, bid-ask spread traversal, market impact, and adverse selection1. Conversely, the Phase 1b daily trend-following rule (Close \> 50-day SMA) deployed on October 1, 2026, occupies a valid macroeconomic risk premium, yet operates near the lower bound of standalone statistical detectability (![][image1] on BTC, ![][image2] on ETH) due to a narrow two-asset universe, binary position sizing, and vulnerability to positive perpetual funding regimes1.

## **Microstructure Forensics: Why the Scalping Engine Failed and How to Repurpose Its Signal**

The post-mortem of the minute-scale scalping engine provides a textbook demonstration of horizon-friction mismatch1. In the first 53 trades prior to the September 24 repair, the account lost \-301.70 USDT and tripped its 3% drawdown circuit breaker because winning trades exited prematurely at a median gross profit of \+11 bps while losing trades timed out at 180 seconds with a median gross loss of \-6.5 bps, against a round-trip taker/maker cost of 8–9 bps1. Following the accounting repairs and exit-rule redesign, the 34-hour clean evidence run (51 trades at 1x leverage, \-70.66 USDT net PnL, 33% win rate) isolated the true underlying expectation of the entry signals: gross return per trade was \+0.15 bps (statistically indistinguishable from zero), maker fees consumed exactly 4.00 bps (0.02% entry \+ 0.02% exit), and net return averaged \-3.85 bps per trade (![][image4])1. Fully 67% of trades terminated via the no-progress timeout, achieving a median Maximum Favorable Excursion (MFE) of just \+3.7 bps—less than the best-case maker-only round-trip fee1.  
![][image5]  
The pre-registered signal study conducted on September 27 across 44,000 five-second feature samples (61 hours) and 120 days of 5-minute candles (440 total hypothesis tests) explains this failure with mathematical finality1. Across all 440 feature-horizon combinations, zero candidates passed the joint discovery (![][image6]), validation (![][image7] with matching sign), and net-of-cost quintile trading gates1. Two distinct microstructural phenomena drove this outcome1. First, the system suffered from autocorrelation inversion at intraday horizons: the 10-indicator conviction and bias scores ported from the CH종합 script exhibited statistically significant negative correlation with forward returns at the 1-to-60 minute holding horizon, posting validation correlations of ![][image8] to ![][image9] and ![][image10]\-statistics down to ![][image11]1. Because lagging technical indicators trigger only after a high-velocity price impulse has already occurred, entering in the direction of the impulse at a 1-to-15 minute horizon systematically buys into liquidity exhaustion and short-term market-maker inventory mean reversion1. Second, the engine encountered sub-friction microstructure alpha: while the depth-5 order-book imbalance ("micro sniper") demonstrated genuine, highly significant positive predictive power over the subsequent 1-minute return (![][image12] on BTC, ![][image13] on ETH), the unconditional 1-minute price dispersion of BTC (1.6 bps) and ETH (2.3 bps) restricted the conditional expected move to roughly 2.0 bps, trapping the signal beneath the 4.0 bps maker-only round-trip fee and 8–9 bps taker/maker hurdle1.

### **Second-Order Architectural Application: Repurposing Order-Book Imbalance as an Execution Layer**

Discarding the depth-5 order-book imbalance signal entirely because it cannot cover round-trip fees as a standalone scalper would waste the strongest statistical predictor discovered in the repository (![][image12] on BTC)1. In institutional quantitative architectures, signals whose horizon expectancy ![][image14] is smaller than round-trip fees (![][image15]) are never traded as standalone alpha; instead, they are deployed as short-horizon execution alpha for implementation shortfall minimization on slower, higher-capacity strategies1.  
Currently, the Phase 1b daily trend-following strategy executes via market (taker) orders immediately upon the 16:00 UTC daily candle close, paying 6.0 bps in Bitget VIP 0 taker fees plus 2–4 bps of bid-ask spread and slippage (\~10 bps per leg, or 20 bps per round trip)1. By repurposing the 5-second feature recorder and depth-5 order-book imbalance predictor (![][image16]) into an Execution Micro-Sniper Module, whenever the daily or multi-hour portfolio engine generates a target position change ![][image17] at 16:00 UTC, the execution module can operate over a 15-to-30 minute execution window ![][image18]1. When executing a buy parent order, the module posts passive Post-Only limit orders at the best bid whenever ![][image19] (absorbing mild selling flow without adverse selection) and crosses the spread or reprices aggressively only if ![][image16] surges above a runaway threshold (![][image20])1.  
Converting a 6.0 bps taker fill plus 4.0 bps slippage (10.0 bps cost) into a 2.0 bps maker fill timed via a ![][image21] 1-minute order-book forecast yields an effective execution improvement of 8.0 to 10.0 bps per trade leg (16 to 20 bps per round trip)1. Across 20 position changes per year, this execution layer alone adds \+2.0% to \+4.0% in risk-free annual compounded equity without taking a single minute of standalone scalping risk1.

## **Econometric Evaluation of the Three Reviewer Questions**

Section 5 of the handoff log poses three foundational questions regarding econometric validation design, small-sample statistical inference, and Pine Script execution semantics1. Each requires a rigorous quantitative resolution.

### **1\. Soundness of the Pre-Registered 60/40 Split on 7 Years of Daily Crypto Data**

The Phase 1 trend study utilized Bitget daily closes from 2019 through September 29, 2026 (2,611 days for BTC, 2,581 days for ETH), partitioned chronologically into the first 60% for discovery (2019 to October 2023\) and the final 40% for out-of-sample validation (November 2023 to September 2026, ![][image22] or 1,058 trading days)1. Pre-registering the exact universe of 16 rules (TSMOM 20/60/120, Price vs SMA 50/100/200, Donchian 20/55, each in long/short and long-only variants) and requiring both a validation Sharpe ![][image23] and ![][image24] of all 16 rules to remain positive in validation is vastly superior to unconstrained backtest optimization1. Notably, 100% of the 16 rules achieved positive net returns in validation on both BTC and ETH, proving that the trend-following premise reflects a broad structural plateau rather than an isolated parameter spike1.  
However, from an institutional econometric standpoint, a single static 60/40 chronological split over a 7-year cryptocurrency history exhibits three critical vulnerabilities1. First, macro-regime non-stationarity separates the two windows: the discovery period (2019–2023) was dominated by retail leverage, unhedged offshore exchange dynamics, the 2020–2021 monetary expansion, and the 2022 credit contagion, whereas the validation period (November 2023–September 2026\) coincided with institutional ETF adoption, compressed realized volatility, tighter basis arbitrage (1.9 bps/day realized Bitget funding versus 9+ bps/day in retail mania), and severe divergence between BTC (+33.1% annualized buy-and-hold) and ETH (+11.2% annualized buy-and-hold)1. A single chronological split therefore conflates out-of-sample generalization with a single macro regime1. Second, low turnover restricts the effective degrees of freedom: because a 50-day moving average rule changes position only 15 times per year on ETH and 23 times per year on BTC, a 2.9-year validation window encompasses only 23 to 35 completed trade clusters, leaving wide confidence intervals around tail metrics such as maximum drawdown1. Third, picking the discovery winner without adjusting for the high collinearity across the 16 moving average, momentum, and breakout rules leaves residual multiple-testing selection bias unquantified9.  
Rather than abandoning pre-registration, the research control plane should replace the single 60/40 split with Anchored Walk-Forward Optimization paired with Hansen's Superior Predictive Ability (SPA) Bootstrap9. Using an initial 2.5-year burn-in (2019–mid-2021), the test evaluates rolling 6-month out-of-sample folds across the remaining 5.2 years (2021–2026), pooling all out-of-sample daily return vectors into a unified 5.2-year out-of-sample record (![][image25]) that spans both the 2022 bear market and the 2024–2026 institutional bull market1. To test whether the selected rule genuinely outperforms a benchmark (either zero return or buy-and-hold) after searching over ![][image26] rules, the gatekeeper should apply Hansen's (2005) SPA test via the Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap (using geometric block lengths ![][image27] to preserve volatility clustering)9:  
![][image28]  
Unlike White's Reality Check (2000), which is overly conservative when inferior rules (such as shorting BTC during a secular bull trend) are included in the candidate pool, Hansen's SPA studentizes each loss differential by its bootstrap standard deviation ![][image29] and recenters the null distribution to exclude manifestly poor rules9.

### **3\. Verification of CH종합 Pine Script Execution Semantics (process\_orders\_on\_close=true)**

The third reviewer question asks whether strategy.exit placed on the entry bar under process\_orders\_on\_close=true in the 3,336-line CH종합 Pine Script behaves as the Python broker emulator port assumes—namely, that stops and targets are erased to na on entries from flat, converted to 0 on the subsequent bar via nz(), leaving longs with no working stop and causing shorts opened from flat to exit immediately one bar later via a buy-stop at 01.  
A forensic trace of TradingView's Pine Script v5/v6 execution model and Broker Emulator confirms that the Python port's reading of the code is completely faithful to standard Pine Script execution semantics when calc\_on\_order\_fills is false (the default), while also revealing why the owner's TradingView chart produced different results1.

#### **Broker Emulator Execution Trace Under Default Settings**

In Pine Script, script evaluation and order matching are strictly separated into two sequential phases at each bar update16. Declaring process\_orders\_on\_close \= true in strategy() instructs the Broker Emulator to fill market orders at the closing tick of Bar ![][image10] rather than the opening tick of Bar ![][image71], but it does not alter the state of built-in position variables during the script's top-to-bottom evaluation pass on Bar ![][image10]16. Suppose the strategy is flat prior to Bar ![][image10] (strategy.position\_size \== 0\)1. At the close of Bar ![][image10], the Pine runtime executes the script from line 1 to line 3,3361. When the entry block triggers and calls strategy.entry(), the command merely places the market order into the Broker Emulator's pending queue to be filled after the script finishes calculating on Bar ![][image10]'s close16. Throughout the remainder of the script's execution on Bar ![][image10], strategy.position\_size remains strictly 0.0 and strategy.position\_avg\_price remains na15.  
Because CH종합 subsequently executes a state-cleanup block conditioned on if strategy.position\_size \== 0 without an entry-bar boolean guard (such as and not justEntered, a known Pine Script anti-pattern documented in strategy engineering15), that conditional evaluates to true on the very bar the entry signal fired, overwriting the newly computed stop\_loss and take\_profit variables back to na1. Once line 3,336 completes on Bar ![][image10], the Broker Emulator processes the queued strategy.entry() order and fills it at close\[t\], at which point strategy.position\_size becomes non-zero16. On Bar ![][image71], strategy.position\_size is now non-zero, so the reset block no longer runs15. However, because CH종합 computes its ATR and assigns its stop/target levels inside the entry-signal conditional block, those variables are not recomputed on Bar ![][image71]; they retain the na value assigned at the bottom of Bar ![][image10]1. When the script passes nz(stop\_loss, 0\) into strategy.exit(..., stop \= nz(stop\_loss, 0)), the Broker Emulator receives a stop order at price 01.  
This stop \= 0 parameter acts asymmetrically on long versus short positions1. On a long position (strategy.position\_size \> 0), stop \= 0 registers a protective sell-stop order at 0.0; because asset prices never fall to 0, the sell-stop never triggers, leaving any long opened from flat completely unprotected until an opposite entry signal reverses the position1. Conversely, on a short position (strategy.position\_size \< 0), a protective stop-loss is a buy-stop order—an instruction to buy back the short if the market price rises to or above the stop trigger price (![][image72])14. When the script submits a buy-stop at stop \= 0 while ETH is trading near \$2,500, the current market price is already higher (worse) than the trigger price of 01. Under TradingView's official Broker Emulator rules, whenever a stop order is submitted at a trigger price that is already worse than the prevailing market price, the emulator immediately executes the order at the very next available tick as a market order, exiting the short one bar after entry1. Only when CH종합 reverses directly from an existing position (strategy.position\_size \!= 0 during Bar ![][image10]'s script pass) is the reset block bypassed and a valid stop retained1.

#### **Reconciling the Owner's Screenshot with the Python Port**

In addition to non-default strategy inputs among the script's \~210 settings, a single TradingView Strategy Properties toggle alters the exact entry-bar wipe described above: calc\_on\_order\_fills \= true, which appears as the checkbox labeled **"After order is filled"** under the *Recalculate* section of the TradingView Strategy Properties UI tab1. If the owner enabled **"After order is filled"** (calc\_on\_order\_fills \= true) in the Properties tab, TradingView executes an extra intrabar script pass on Bar ![][image10] immediately after strategy.entry() fills at close\[t\]14. During that second execution pass on Bar ![][image10], the entry condition remains true on close\[t\], and strategy.position\_size is now non-zero (\!= 0\)14. Consequently, during that immediate post-fill recalculation pass on Bar ![][image10], the script recalculates the stop and target inside the entry block, skips the if strategy.position\_size \== 0 reset wipe, and registers the valid strategy.exit() bracket order before Bar ![][image71] ever begins14.  
Furthermore, the second defect identified in CH종합—computing ta.atr() inside conditional blocks—triggers a classic Pine v4/v5 runtime divergence1. Since Pine v4, expressions inside unselected branches of conditional blocks are not executed on every bar; when stateful rolling functions like ta.atr() (which relies on an internal Wilder smoothing state) are evaluated conditionally, their internal accumulator only steps forward on signal bars, yielding a heavily lagged, stale volatility estimate compared to a global ta.atr() call1.

## **Resolution of Open Infrastructure and Runtime Anomalies**

Before scaling the system across multiple assets or re-enabling autonomous research loops, the three unresolved infrastructure anomalies logged in Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the handoff report must be permanently engineered out of the host environment1.

### **1\. Root Cause and Fix for the 35-Second Silent WebSocket Feed Gaps ("G1" Gate Failure)**

During the 34-hour continuity check ("G1"), the Bitget market data stream went completely silent 19 times for durations up to 35 seconds without raising a WebSocket disconnect exception1. This failure arises from a protocol mismatch between standard Python WebSocket libraries, OS TCP retransmission timers, and Bitget's application-layer edge gateway20. Specifically, Python's websockets library maintains connection health via RFC 6455 control frames (0x9 Ping / 0xA Pong), sending a ping every 20 seconds and waiting another 20 seconds for a pong before terminating the socket (40 seconds total detection latency)22. However, Bitget's Unified Trading Account (UTA) and Classic WebSocket gateways operate on an application-level text heartbeat, requiring the client to transmit the literal string "ping" every 30 seconds to receive "pong", and severing idle connections after 120 seconds20. When an intermediate NAT router, ISP node, or cloud ingress load balancer drops state or experiences packet loss without transmitting a TCP RST or FIN packet, the local Windows socket remains in an ESTABLISHED state while the OS kernel enters exponential TCP retransmission backoff (1s \+ 2s \+ 4s \+ 8s \+ 16s \= 31s)22. During this 31-to-35 second window, await ws.recv() blocks silently without throwing ConnectionClosed, blinding the trading runner and causing the G1 continuity gate to fail1.  
Eliminating these silent gaps requires deploying a Dual-Socket Active/Standby Multiplexer with an aggressive application-layer watchdog20. Every ws.recv() call should be wrapped in an asyncio.wait\_for timeout of ![][image75], paired with a background coroutine that sends the literal string "ping" every 15 seconds20. Because high-liquidity pairs like BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT emit public order-book depth and ticker updates every 100–500 ms, five seconds of silence is an unambiguous indicator of a stalled TCP pipe1. Furthermore, maintaining two concurrent, independent WebSocket connections (Conn\_A and Conn\_B, staggered in initialization by 15 seconds) subscribed to the same Bitget channels and feeding a sequence-deduplicated ring buffer guarantees uninterrupted continuity: if Conn\_A stalls for more than 3.0 seconds, Conn\_B seamlessly supplies ticks while Conn\_A reconnects in the background alongside an immediate asynchronous REST snapshot poll1.

### **2\. Root Cause and Fix for the 30–50 Minute Stalls, 5–15s Page Faults, and RAM Shifts**

Since October 2, 2026, the stall monitor logged 425 events: most lasted 5–15 seconds (characterized by page faults with zero garbage collection time), while several lasted 30–50 minutes, alongside unlogged restarts on October 13 (22:22, 22:29) and October 14 (06:19), and a shift in reported total system RAM from 11.8 GB to 14.8 GB1.  
On a Windows 11 desktop host, launching pythonw.exe via wscript.exe at user logon runs the server in a background user session that does not inhibit the Windows Power Manager1. When the interactive user steps away and the system idle timer elapses, Windows transitions the host into S0 Low Power Idle (Modern Standby) or S3 Sleep, suspending all user-mode threads (pythonw.exe) without terminating the process1. Upon wake 30 to 50 minutes later, the elapsed clock delta inside the stall monitor registers a massive 30–50 minute stall, while the 06:19 restart (matching a 06:18 OS boot) and the 22:22 / 22:29 restarts reflect Windows Update reboots or session logoffs1. Simultaneously, the shift in OS-reported total RAM from 11.8 GB to 14.8 GB on a 16 GB Windows 11 machine occurs when an integrated GPU (UMA shared aperture) or hypervisor subsystem dynamically releases reserved physical memory back to the OS kernel1. Even with a 320 MB minimum working-set request, Windows 11 aggressively trims idle private pages of background pythonw.exe processes to the NVMe pagefile during long periods of low CPU activity; when the 30-minute research check or feature rotation triggers disk I/O, faulting those trimmed pages back from disk blocks the single-threaded asyncio event loop for 5–15 seconds1.  
To permanently resolve both host sleep and page-fault stalls, the startup sequence in main.py should invoke the Win32 execution-state API via a pre-allocated ctypes function pointer (strictly avoiding dynamic ctypes.Structure creation inside loops, which caused the earlier 30 MB/hr memory leak)1: calling ctypes.windll.kernel32.SetThreadExecutionState(0x80000000 | 0x00000001 | 0x00000040) (ES\_CONTINUOUS | ES\_SYSTEM\_REQUIRED | ES\_AWAYMODE\_REQUIRED) instructs the Windows kernel that the process is performing time-critical background execution and forbids S0/S3 sleep while permitting the display to power down23. In tandem, the live runner, WebSocket feed, and 5-second feature recorder must be isolated in a lightweight process (rsquant\_live.exe, footprint \< 80 MB) with SQLite configured in Write-Ahead Logging mode (PRAGMA journal\_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA mmap\_size=268435456;), while the P1/P2 research controller and deterministic replay engine execute in a separate worker process spawned at BELOW\_NORMAL\_PRIORITY\_CLASS1.

### **Three Structural Synergies of the Bitget Multi-Asset Stack**

#### **1\. The Fundamental Law of Active Management (Solving the ![][image76] Bottleneck)**

By Grinold's Fundamental Law of Active Management, the portfolio Sharpe ratio ![][image77] of a systematic rule applied across ![][image78] assets with individual Sharpe ratios ![][image79] and average pairwise strategy-return correlation ![][image80] is:  
![][image81]  
When Phase 1 tested 12 additional cryptocurrency altcoins, the median Sharpe was only \+0.27 and cross-crypto correlation during macro drawdowns approached ![][image82], offering negligible diversification during the 2022 crash1. In contrast, combining four distinct macro clusters available on Bitget—Crypto Majors (BTC, ETH, SOL), Tokenized U.S. Secular Growth Equities (NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, QQQ, SPY), Safe-Haven & Commodity CFDs (XAUUSD Gold, Crude Oil), and Major FX CFDs (EURUSD, USDJPY)—yields a cross-asset trend-following portfolio where average pairwise strategy-return correlation drops to ![][image83]4. Even if individual asset net Sharpe ratios average only ![][image84] across ![][image85] multi-asset instruments, the portfolio Sharpe ratio expands to:  
![][image86]  
Historically, during the 2022 crypto bear market where the long-only 50-day SMA rule lost \-51% on BTC and \-36% on ETH, energy commodities, the U.S. Dollar, and short equity/bond trends generated substantial positive trend returns, smoothing the combined equity curve and eliminating multi-year stagnation1.

#### **2\. Dynamic Funding-Aware Instrument Routing (Solving the 9 bps/day Stress Failure)**

Phase 1 proved that the BTC trend rule passes at base funding (3 bps/day, or 10.95%/year), but fails at bull-market stress funding (9 bps/day, or 32.85%/year)1. Paying 32.85% annualized funding to hold an unlevered (1x) long perpetual position is an avoidable structural drag1. Because RS-Quant operates at 1x unlevered notional (5,000 USDT per coin on a 10,000 USDT account)1, the execution router should implement a Funding-Threshold Venue Switch between Bitget's perpetual and spot order books2. When the 3-day exponentially weighted moving average of Bitget's 8-hour funding rate remains at or below 0.010% (3.0 bps/day), long trend signals execute on USDT-M Perpetuals to capture the lower transaction fee (2 bps maker / 6 bps taker versus 8 bps spot with the 20% BGB deduction, or 5.6 bps with an added 30% affiliate fee rebate)1. Conversely, whenever bull-market euphoria drives the 3-day average 8-hour funding rate above 0.015% (4.5 bps/day) while the daily trend signal remains long (Close \> SMA\_50), the router automatically migrates the 1x long position from the USDT-M Perpetual book to the Bitget Spot Book, paying a one-time switch cost of \~8–10 bps and 0.00 bps/day in ongoing funding thereafter1. Within three days of elevated funding, the Spot switch amortizes its transaction cost and completely immunizes the trend strategy against the 9 bps/day bull-market funding stress failure1.

#### **3\. Regime-Conditional Cross-Asset Collateral & Basis Carry Overlay**

Although standalone funding-rate carry (Phase 2\) was set aside because unhedged or statically allocated carry yields only 5%–9% gross per year during calm markets, Bitget's funding rate history shows that funding is positive 79%–95% of the time1. Instead of running carry as a separate static silo, RS-Quant should deploy Dead-Capital Carry Recycling: whenever the daily trend-following strategy is flat on BTC or ETH (Close \< SMA\_50), the idle 5,000 USDT allocation does not sit at 0% yield1. If the trailing 24-hour funding rate on BTCUSDT or ETHUSDT is positive (![][image87]), the system deploys the idle capital into a delta-neutral Long Spot \+ Short USDT-M Perpetual basis position (executed via passive maker limit orders at 2 bps futures \+ 5.6 bps spot net fee), harvesting the 5%–9%+ annualized funding rate while waiting for the next Close \> SMA\_50 trend breakout1. Furthermore, on the equity leg, Bitget allows investors to hold Tokenized U.S. Stocks (capturing long equity momentum at 0% funding and 0.04%–0.05% StockRoute fees) and pledge those tokenized shares as collateral to borrow stablecoins without selling the equity position, enabling capital-efficient cross-margining across both equity and crypto trend signals5.

## **Blueprint for a Dynamic, Self-Recursively Improving System (RS-Quant v2.0)**

The central architectural challenge is making RS-Quant dynamically and self-recursively improving without succumbing to the backtest overfitting and parameter thrashing that plagued the initial scalper1. In the September 24 audit, the P1/P2 DeepSeek research loop failed because multiple components mutated the same flat parameters, premature runs on 12 minutes of data poisoned the "rejected ideas" prompt history, and the LLM was restricted to tweaking scalar constants (like atr\_target\_mult or order-book thresholds) inside a hard-coded strategy structure1. True recursive self-improvement requires separating fast parametric adaptation—which must be governed by continuous convex mathematics—from slow structural evolution, where an LLM acts as a symbolic hypothesis generator subject to strict multiple-testing econometric gates1.  
![][image88]

### **Tier 0: Self-Calibrating Microstructure Execution & Cost Surface Loop (Timescale: Seconds to Hours)**

Tier 0 operates inside the isolated real-time runner and improves execution efficiency autonomously without mutating strategy logic1. Every order submitted by RS-Quant logs its depth-5 order-book imbalance decile ![][image89], prevailing bid-ask spread width, time-to-fill, and realized slippage against the arrival mid-price1. An Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) continuously updates the expected maker fill probability ![][image90] and expected taker slippage ![][image91] per instrument. Using the depth-5 order-book imbalance signal (![][image12] BTC, ![][image92] ETH)1, Tier 0 slices parent portfolio rebalance orders into passive Post-Only maker orders whenever expected adverse selection sits below the 4.0 bps maker-vs-taker fee savings (0.06% \- 0.02% \= 0.04% on VIP 0, or 0.028% with a 30% rebate), dynamically recalibrating its urgency threshold as Bitget order-book liquidity fluctuates across sessions1.

### **Tier 1: Continuous Volatility-Targeted & Funding-Penalized Portfolio Engine (Timescale: Daily / 4-Hourly)**

The Phase 1b production rule currently uses a binary step function (![][image93] based on Close \> SMA\_50) with a static 5,000 USDT allocation per coin and a 50% emergency circuit breaker1. Binary rules suffer from severe whipsaw risk when price oscillates around the 50-day average—as demonstrated by the first closed ETH paper trade (-522.83 USDT or \-10.5% loss when ETH entered at 2,710.94 on October 1 and exited at 2,434.12 after dipping below the 2,546.10 SMA)1. Furthermore, sizing BTC and ETH equally in notional dollars (5,000 USDT each) allocates unequal risk because ETH's realized volatility is 25%–35% higher than BTC's (124 bps vs 97 bps typical daily move)1.  
Tier 1 replaces binary step sizing with a continuous, self-scaling portfolio law. Instead of a single 50-day crossover that flips allocation from 0% to 100% on a 1-bp price change, the engine computes a multi-horizon continuous trend forecast ![][image94] by blending three exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) crossover speeds—Fast (16/64), Medium (32/128, matching the 50-day SMA center of mass), and Slow (64/256)—normalized by the instrument's 25-day daily return standard deviation ![][image95] and clipped smoothly to ![][image96] for long-only venues (or ![][image97] where shorting is validated):  
![][image98]  
To account for carry drag, the engine adjusts the raw forecast by subtracting the annualized funding rate ratio when trading perpetuals (or routes directly to Spot / Tokenized Equities when funding exceeds 4.5 bps/day)1:  
![][image99]  
Each asset's target weight ![][image100] is then scaled inversely to its real-time exponentially weighted annualized volatility ![][image101] toward a portfolio target volatility ![][image102] (such as 25% annualized), multiplied by a cross-asset diversification multiplier ![][image103]:  
![][image104]  
When crypto enters a high-volatility crash regime (as in 2022), ![][image101] spikes automatically, forcing ![][image100] down before the moving average even crosses and replacing the blunt 50% static circuit breaker with smooth, continuous drawdown control1. Finally, consistent with the Phase 1 check-frequency study—which proved that checking signals every 4 hours or 1 hour increased trades from 23 to 106/year and cut BTC Sharpe from 0.96 to 0.511—rebalances execute only at the 16:00 UTC daily close and only when the divergence between the current weight ![][image105] and optimal target weight ![][image100] exceeds a 10% no-trade inertia buffer:  
![][image106]

### **Tier 2: Out-of-Process Deterministic Replay & Econometric Gatekeeper (Timescale: Weekly / Event-Driven)**

Tier 2 upgrades the P1/P2 research controller so that every candidate modification must survive a four-stage econometric gauntlet in an isolated worker process before promotion to production1. In the first stage (Pre-Flight Data Sufficiency and Epistemic Hygiene), the controller verifies that the recorded feature surface (EVIDENCE\_SOURCE \== RECORDED\_SURFACE or verified multi-year multi-asset history) contains enough independent trade clusters (![][image107] across the asset pool) to mathematically clear the statistical gates1. If the sample is insufficient, the cycle exits with status DEFERRED\_INSUFFICIENT\_POWER without consuming the daily experiment budget and without writing to the rejected-ideas memory, permanently preventing the epistemic contamination discovered on September 251.  
In the second stage (Multi-Regime Stress Accounting), every candidate replay applies exact Decimal round-trip fees, conservative slippage modeled from Tier 0's empirical distribution, and a Dual-Funding Stress Check requiring positive net expectancy under both base historical funding (3 bps/day) and 90th-percentile bull-market stress funding (9 bps/day), which automatically enforces Spot and Tokenized-Equity routing1. In the third stage (Cumulative Deflated Sharpe Ratio Gate), the database maintains an append-only counter ![][image108] of every experiment ever evaluated on the validation set1. As the research plane evaluates dozens of experiments over months, the false-positive hurdle ![][image109] automatically rises logarithmically via the extreme-value theorem formula, requiring a candidate to achieve ![][image110]3. In the fourth stage (Hansen's SPA Bootstrap Over Incumbent), a candidate policy ![][image111] is promoted over the live incumbent policy ![][image112] if and only if its out-of-sample daily net return differential ![][image113] achieves a Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap p-value ![][image114] under Hansen's SPA test9.

### **Tier 3: Epistemic Memory Graph & Agentic Symbolic Alpha Architect (Timescale: Monthly)**

The DeepSeek LLM failed to uncover an edge in September 2026 because it was confined to parameter space exploration—proposing scalar adjustments like atr\_target\_mult: 1.8 or ob\_threshold: 0.42 inside a structurally flawed minute-scalping template1. Gradient-free numerical optimization over a handful of floats is far better handled by convex math or Bayesian optimization; where an LLM possesses genuine comparative advantage is constrained symbolic hypothesis generation across structural factor space1.  
To enable structural self-improvement, Tier 3 replaces raw PnL feedback with a Structured Epistemic Ledger that decomposes closed trades and missed opportunities across volatility regimes (high/low ATR percentile), funding regimes (![][image115], ![][image116], ![][image117]), cross-asset dispersion, and excursion efficiency (![][image118] and ![][image119] distributions)1. Every prior hypothesis is logged under a classified failure taxonomy—distinguishing REJECTED\_GROSS\_EDGE\_ZERO (no predictive power), REJECTED\_TURNOVER\_COST\_DRAG (positive gross alpha consumed by Bitget fees or funding), and REJECTED\_COLLINEAR\_REDUNDANT (passes standalone, but exhibits ![][image120] correlation with the incumbent portfolio and adds zero incremental SPA value)1.  
Guided by this diagnostic ledger, DeepSeek proposes candidate alpha factors and regime filters not by editing raw Python code or tuning 210 unconstricted parameters like CH종합, but by composing parsimonious symbolic trees (restricted to a maximum tree depth of 3 operators and ![][image121] free parameters) drawn from a verified Domain-Specific Language (DSL) of time-series and cross-sectional primitives: ts\_zscore(x, d), ts\_rank(x, d), ewma\_diff(x, fast, slow), cross\_sectional\_rank(x), realized\_vol\_ratio(short\_w, long\_w), funding\_term\_zscore(symbol, w), ob\_imbalance\_ema(symbol, w), and lead\_lag\_beta(target\_asset, driver\_asset, w) (which captures cross-market spillovers, such as whether U.S. Tokenized Tech Equity QQQ/NVDA momentum during New York trading hours leads BTC/ETH drift during the subsequent Asian session on Bitget)1. When a symbolic factor generated by Tier 3 passes all four econometric gates in Tier 2, it joins an Ensemble Strategy Book as an orthogonal sleeve rather than overwriting the incumbent rule. A meta-allocator then adjusts the capital weight ![][image122] of each active sleeve using Discounted Exponentially Weighted Multiplicative Weights (Regret Minimization) with hard floor and ceiling bounds, smoothly shifting capital toward sleeves whose realized out-of-sample Information Ratio tracks their pre-registered expectation while automatically quarantining any sleeve whose rolling 90-day return breaches its 99% bootstrap lower confidence bound.

### **Strategic Synthesis for System Evolution**

Preserving the running Phase 1b paper baseline (BTC long, ETH flat, 9,428.21 USDT equity) is essential to accumulate forward observational evidence while infrastructure hardening takes place1. The single closed ETH trade (-522.83 USDT, or \-10.5%) represents a normal trend-following whipsaw and carries no statistical weight against the 7-year historical validation record1. Immediate priority belongs to patching the Windows sleep state via SetThreadExecutionState and deploying the 15-second application "ping" / 5-second stale-tick dual-socket switchover so that the 24-hour G1 feed-continuity gate passes without silent drops1.  
In parallel, closing the forensic investigation of CH종합 requires inspecting the owner's TradingView Properties and Inputs screenshots—specifically verifying whether After order is filled (calc\_on\_order\_fills \= true) is enabled and checking short-from-flat trades in the List of Trades for 1-bar stop-at-zero exits—and then evaluating the exact matched configuration strictly on the 2019–2023 out-of-sample period that the free TradingView plan could not display1. If the 210 parameters degrade out-of-sample on 2019–2023, the monolithic script should be retired in favor of extracting low-complexity indicator primitives into the Tier 3 Symbolic DSL1. Ultimately, durable compounding on Bitget will not emerge from forcing 1-minute noise through 8 bps of exchange friction, nor from trading two coins 15 times a year with binary 100% / 0% step switches1. It will be achieved by combining continuous, volatility-targeted trend and carry forecasts across Bitget's weakly correlated Crypto, Tokenized Equity, and TradFi venues, routing around elevated perpetual funding via the Spot and Tokenized Stock books, executing rebalances passively through the depth-5 order-book micro-sniper, and governing all structural LLM discoveries through cumulative Deflated Sharpe and Hansen SPA statistical gates1.
